required_fixes: Convert purely generic restatements into entity-specific disclosures where evidence exists: explicitly identify the reporting entity, the related financial statements (which statements and period), and confirm the sustainability disclosures cover the same period and are reported at the same time (IFRS S1.20, .22, .64).
State the presentation currency used in sustainability-related financial disclosures and confirm it matches the financial statements’ presentation currency (IFRS S1.24).
Add an entity-specific explanation of how the entity assessed whether additional information beyond specifically applicable IFRS SDS was necessary, and what was done (IFRS S1.15(b)).

Disclose the specific standards/pronouncements/other guidance applied (e.g., SASB topics/metrics considered, other methodologies used) and identify the industry(s) applied for selecting topics/metrics (IFRS S1.55, .58, .59(a), .59(b)).

If cross-referencing is used, specify what information is incorporated by cross-reference, to which report/location, and confirm compliance with B45–B47; if not used, state that cross-referencing is not used (IFRS S1.63).
State whether comparative information is provided for all amounts and, where useful, for narrative/descriptive information (IFRS S1.70).
Disclose the most significant non-measurement judgements made in preparing the sustainability-related financial disclosures (IFRS S1.74).

Tie the IFRS S1 objective to the entity’s identified sustainability-related risks/opportunities and their expected effects on cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital, using available scenario/capital/financial summary evidence (IFRS S1.3).

Reframe the section from a generic restatement of IFRS S1 into a basis-of-preparation narrative that explains how the reporting entity prepares and presents its sustainability-related financial disclosures in alignment with IFRS S1 and S2.

Introduce a short opening paragraph that states the scope and purpose of the section (e.g., that it sets out the basis of preparation, reporting boundary, connectivity to financial statements, and use of estimates and judgements).

Adopt a consistent numbered heading structure (e.g., 1. General requirements; 1.1 Objective and scope; 1.2 Fair presentation; 1.3 Materiality; 1.4 Reporting entity; 1.5 Connected information; 1.6 Core content; 1.7 Sources of guidance; 1.8 Location of disclosures).

For each subsection, add a one-sentence purpose statement that explains why the topic matters for reading this report (e.g., "This subsection describes how we determine which sustainability-related risks and opportunities are material for these disclosures.").

Shift the voice so that externally defined requirements are described in neutral third-person ("IFRS S1 requires...") but are immediately followed by first-person plural statements describing how the entity applies them (e.g., "We apply these requirements by...").

Avoid copying or closely paraphrasing IFRS S1 clause wording; instead, summarize requirements in your own words while maintaining technical accuracy and referencing the standard in parentheses where needed.

Introduce bullets that describe the entity’s qualitative characteristics and preparation principles (e.g., completeness, neutrality, accuracy, comparability, verifiability, timeliness, understandability) and how they are operationalized in the report.

Add explicit cross-reference placeholders to related sections (e.g., "Refer to [Section: Governance]" for governance disclosures, "Refer to [Section: Strategy]" for strategy, etc.) to support connectivity and navigability.

Include a short explanation of how the reporting boundary for sustainability-related financial disclosures aligns with the financial statements, including treatment of value chain information where relevant.

Add content on estimates, judgements, and data limitations consistent with the missing data protocol: explain where information may be incomplete or under development, why, what interim approaches are used, and the planned direction of enhancement, using standardized labels such as "not applicable", "not material", or "not currently available" where appropriate.

Clarify how the entity uses sources of guidance such as IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards and SASB Standards in practice (e.g., how topics and metrics are identified and when topics/metrics are deemed not applicable), rather than only stating that the standards may be referred to.
Where lists of requirements or characteristics are presented, ensure parallel grammar and use of standards-oriented verbs (e.g., "identify", "assess", "measure", "monitor", "disclose").

Consider adding a compact mapping table that links each general requirement topic (e.g., fair presentation, materiality, connected information) to the relevant sections of the report, with a clear caption and reference in the narrative.

Close the section with a brief connectivity statement summarizing how these general requirements link to the detailed disclosures under Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, and Metrics and Targets, using generic cross-reference placeholders.

section_generation_score.policy: Missing requirements reduce audit/readiness visibility only; they must not appear in report prose.
